payload.recallText: I began my illustrious career in journalism as a reporter, writing articles for the Ram, the school newspaper at Fordham University.  One day I was out walking on campus and I saw the Dean walking by.  The Dean was promoting a program to bring more elite, well bred and rich students to campus.  Being an ambitious reporter, I whipped out my notebook and my pen and I approached him.  "Dean, tell me about how your program will increase the tuition rates at Fordham college faster than the rate of inflation."  He looked straight at me and said, "Shut up, Punk."  That's when I saw the other man.  And I noticed that he was holding something with cream in it.  And then he was standing right next to me.  And then he was throwing the pie that he held into the Dean's face. "Dean, would you care to comment on this latest attack?"  "Fuck you, " he said and then walked away.  I ran straight to the office of the Ram to tell my editor about this lead.  My editor's name was Jim Dwyer.  Jim went on to win a Pulitzer prize, and that's the truth.  "The Dean?  That man is a dick.  Write it up!"  he said.  So I did.  I sat down and I wrote out the details about what happened.  And then I started to embellish them.  Most reporters draw the line at making up facts, but I felt an impulse to do it so I did.  The first thing that I did was call the attacker Pie Man.  Then I reported that he was wearing a cape, and used alliterative words to describe how it flapped in the wind as he ran away.  I showed it to my editor.  "Pie Man?  I love it!  First page!"  And that's how it began.  Soon, I received a note.  "I loved your article.  Want to see me in action again?  Come to the library tomorrow afternoon at <insert time>. Signed, Pie Man."  The next day I showed up at the assigned time to see Sheila, the student body president.  Sheila was one of the types of students that the Dean wanted to bring to Fordham university.  She was well to do and she knew it.  She wasn't very nice.  So when Pie Man attacked her, I reveled in writing it up.  I again used the name Pie Man and described his cape and included other narrative details.  Soon, everyone around campus was talking about Pie Man.  People were even dressing up in capes, like the Pie Man I portrayed in my articles.  The Ram featured five articles about Pie Man all in all.  And all five articles were written by me.  One night I was out at a bar and I noticed Angela was there also.  Angela was a girl that I had a crush on.  I had a crush on her, but I didn't think she even knew my name.  So imagine my shock when she came up to me.  "Jim, my friends and I were just talking about you.  We all think that you are Pie Man because you always know where Pie Man is going to be.  So are you?"  She asked this question in a way that I knew that she would have sex with me if I answered in the affirmative.  Now, I wasn't Pie Man.  But, I had created Pie Man, hadn't I?  By writing him up in the newspaper and giving him a name and a costume, I had created his character.  Hadn't I?  So I answered her, "Yes, I am Pie Man."  "Oh good," she said, "I'm glad that we figured that out!"
